title: Operator-guard the 4 agent-called write routes once pof-mcp sends a token
body:
## Summary
catalog/step-submit, catalog/lifecycle, pipeline and drain/settle-test POSTs still run without requireOperator because their header-less agent callers (pof-mcp pofClient, cli-task @@CALLBACK) present no token.

## Description
src/lib/api-auth.ts:6-12 names artifact writes and lifecycle transitions privileged. After efdadb2d the filesystem-derived guard test (src/__tests__/api/catalog-pipeline-operator-guard.test.ts) holds these four as reasoned EXEMPT entries. tools/pof-mcp/src/pofClient.ts:40 sends only Content-Type, so guarding them today breaks pof_submit_artifact / pof_ue_run_tests the moment POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN is set. Fixed = pofClient (and the cli-task callback) forward POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN as Authorization: Bearer, then the four routes call requireOperator first and the EXEMPT map empties (its stale-entry test then forces removal).

## Flow
- pofClient reads POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN from env and sets Authorization
- cli-task callback POST carries the same header
- add requireOperator to the 4 routes before the body read
- delete the 4 EXEMPT entries; guard test stays green

## Expected impact
A cross-site text/plain POST can no longer submit artifacts, sync lifecycle or settle gates; with a token configured the agent loop keeps working. Could break: any out-of-tree script POSTing these routes under token mode.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every catalog->UE write handler gated
Before: 4 write handlers unguarded (EXEMPT map in the guard test)
After: 0 unguarded; pof-mcp contract tests green with a token set
Method: simulation - walked pofClient.ts:40 and the 4 handlers; the A/B needs pof-mcp's own test runner plus a token-mode run, outside this round's paths
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: guard test EXEMPT map empty + tools/pof-mcp node --test suite green with POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN set, both arms

title: Allow-list drain-python's caller-supplied bridgeUrl to loopback
body:
## Summary
POST /api/pipeline-artifacts/drain-python takes bridgeUrl from the request body and the server fetches it (runPython -> bridgeFetch): a server-side request to any host the caller names.

## Description
src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/drain-python/route.ts passes body.bridgeUrl to makeDeps -> runPython(module, fn, {}, { bridgeUrl }) and src/lib/bridge/run-python.ts:135 fetches `opts.bridgeUrl ?? DEFAULT_BRIDGE_URL`. The route is now operator-guarded (efdadb2d), which closes the CSRF vector but not an SSRF from an operator/agent-supplied value. Fixed = accept only http(s)://localhost|127.0.0.1|[::1] with a port, else 400.

## Flow
- POST drain-python { bridgeUrl: 'http://169.254.169.254/' }
- route -> runPython -> bridgeFetch to that host
- fix: parse URL, refuse non-loopback hostnames with 400 before any fetch

## Expected impact
The drain cannot be pointed at an arbitrary network host. Could break: an operator running the editor bridge on a LAN machine (would need an explicit allow-list env).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - server fetches only the local bridge
Before: any host accepted
After: non-loopback -> 400, loopback unchanged
Method: simulation - traced body.bridgeUrl to bridgeFetch; a route test with a mocked runPython decides it (S), deferred because the remote-editor use case is an operator call
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/drain-python/route.ts:96 makeDeps(typeof body.bridgeUrl === 'string' ? body.bridgeUrl : undefined)
src/lib/bridge/run-python.ts:135 bridgeFetch<unknown>(opts.bridgeUrl ?? DEFAULT_BRIDGE_URL, {
instrument: route test with mocked runPython: non-loopback bridgeUrl -> 400 and runPython not called; grep scripts/ for any LAN bridge configuration

title: Compare the operator token in constant time
body:
## Summary
requireOperator compares the presented token with `!==`, an early-exit comparison that leaks matched-prefix length through timing.

## Description
src/lib/api-auth.ts:42 `if (presented !== token)`. Registry authorization/dispatch-chokepoint-gating: the channel proof is compared in constant time. Fixed = crypto.timingSafeEqual over equal-length Buffers (length mismatch -> reject). Out of this context's paths (api-auth belongs to Application Infrastructure).

## Flow
- read POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN
- Buffer.from both, reject on length mismatch
- timingSafeEqual

## Expected impact
Token-mode deployments stop leaking prefix timing. Nothing user-visible changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - constant-time token check
Before: 1 early-exit compare
After: 0
Method: simulation - read src/lib/api-auth.ts:42; api-auth.test.ts would pin it, out of scope here
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: src/__tests__/lib/api-auth.test.ts green on both arms + a source assertion that timingSafeEqual is used

title: Take the drain lease before a revision restore
body:
## Summary
POST /api/pipeline-artifacts/revisions restores a step's live row with no drain lease, so a restore during an in-flight drain can be overwritten by the drain's write-back for the same entity.

## Description
settle-test takes the same lease as /drain for the scope it writes (src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/drain/settle-test/route.ts:40-44); the revisions POST (src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/revisions/route.ts) commits via commitArtifact with no lease. A drain applying a verdict to the row the operator just restored can silently replace the restored data/verdict. Fixed = acquireLeases(leaseKeysForFilter({catalogId, entityId})) around the commit, 409 when held (dry run exempt).

## Flow
- drain starts on items/sword
- operator restores a revision of items/sword
- drain's applyVerdict upserts over the restored row

## Expected impact
A restore can no longer be clobbered mid-drain; the operator sees a 409 naming the in-flight drain. Could break: a restore attempted during a long global drain now has to wait.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - restore and drain mutually exclusive per entity
Before: 0 lease checks on restore
After: 409 while a lease is held
Method: simulation - two routes walked; a test acquiring a lease then POSTing a restore decides it
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/drain/settle-test/route.ts:40 const keys = leaseKeysForFilter(filter);
src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/revisions/route.ts:80 const committed = commitArtifact(
instrument: route test: acquireLeases for items/sword then POST restore -> expect 409 and no upsert; release -> 200

title: Validate drain-python's boolean flags instead of truthiness
body:
## Summary
drain-python reads `apply: body.apply !== false`, so `apply: "false"` or `0` APPLIES writes; force/continueOnFail use `=== true`, so the same string silently means no.

## Description
src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/drain-python/route.ts POST: `{ apply: body.apply !== false, force: body.force === true, continueOnFail: body.continueOnFail === true }`. A caller that serialises a dry run as a string gets a live apply against the editor. Fixed = each flag, when present, must be boolean (400 otherwise) - the shape the drain-worker knobs got in cc954cd5.

## Flow
- POST drain-python { apply: 'false' }
- route applies every re-graded step

## Expected impact
A mistyped dry run can no longer write. Could break: none in-tree (no caller sends these as strings).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - non-boolean flags refused
Before: apply:'false' -> live apply
After: 400
Method: simulation - read the expression; a 3-case route test (mocked drainPythonAll) decides it
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/drain-python/route.ts:100 { apply: body.apply !== false, force: body.force === true, continueOnFail: body.continueOnFail === true }
instrument: route test with mocked drainPythonAll: {apply:'false'} -> 400, {apply:false} -> called with apply false

title: Move toStepSummary out of components/ so the summary API route does not import UI code
body:
## Summary
GET /api/pipeline-artifacts/summary imports its projection from @/components/layout-lab/stepSummary - a server route depending on the component tree.

## Description
src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts/summary/route.ts:4 imports toStepSummary from '@/components/layout-lab/stepSummary'. The projection is pure data shaping shared by the lab and the route; living under components/ means a client-only import added to that module (or its transitive imports) lands in the server route. Fixed = move to src/lib/catalog/stepSummary.ts and re-export from the old path. Owned by the sibling catalog-pipeline-state context (layout-lab), so not built here.

## Flow
- grep imports of layout-lab/stepSummary
- git mv to src/lib/catalog/
- leave a re-export at the old path

## Expected impact
The route no longer pulls component-tree modules. Could break: nothing while the re-export stays.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - API route imports 0 component modules
Before: 1 route import from src/components (grep of src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts)
After: 0
Method: simulation - grep of src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts for '@/components' = 1 hit
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: grep -rn '@/components' src/app/api/pipeline-artifacts = 0 + summary route test green

title: Answer GET /api/catalog for an unregistered catalog with 404 like its siblings
body:
## Summary
GET /api/catalog?catalogId=<typo> returns 200 [] while /api/catalog/entities and /api/catalog/lifecycle answer the same id with 404 CatalogNotFoundError.

## Description
src/app/api/catalog/route.ts:14-18 returns listLifecycle(catalogId) for any id; src/app/api/catalog/entities/route.ts:16 and src/app/api/catalog/lifecycle/route.ts:28 map CatalogNotFoundError to 404. A typo'd catalogId reads as 'no entities yet' on one surface and 'no such catalog' on the other. Fixed = 404 when neither the pipeline registry nor the lifecycle table knows the id (keep [] for a known catalog with no rows); unregistered synthetic catalogs (loot-filter) may legitimately hold rows.

## Flow
- GET /api/catalog?catalogId=itemz
- 200 [] (silent)
- GET /api/catalog/entities?catalogId=itemz -> 404

## Expected impact
Typos surface. Could break: a caller that relies on [] for unknown ids (lab hydration) - consumers need a grep first.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one answer for an unknown catalog across 3 sibling routes
Before: 1 of 3 routes says 200 []
After: 3 of 3 say 404
Method: simulation - read the 3 handlers; consumer survey not done
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
evidence:
src/app/api/catalog/route.ts:18 return apiSuccess(listLifecycle(catalogId));
src/app/api/catalog/entities/route.ts:16 if (e instanceof CatalogNotFoundError) return apiError(e.message, 404);
instrument: grep consumers of GET /api/catalog?catalogId; route test unknown id -> 404, synthetic loot-filter id with rows -> 200
